inference.step: Three officers of Humphreys's division, writing within 45 days, give three hours for their own units: Brewster (Second Brigade) about midnight, Humphreys (division, end of the march) 1 a.m., Tripp and Bodine (11th Massachusetts and 26th Pennsylvania of the First Brigade) 2 a.m. The window from the earliest to the latest is shown; whether they are the head, middle and tail of one column is not said by any of them and is not claimed.

weighing.summary: The plan lists midnight and 02:00 and recommends 02:00. Four officers of the division wrote within 45 days. Brewster, commanding the Second Brigade, wrote 15 Aug 1863 that his brigade marched through Emmitsburg to a point near Gettysburg, 'reaching there about midnight' (the antecedent of 'there' is read, not stated). Humphreys wrote 16 Aug that the division was 'bivouacking at 1 a. m. on July 2 about 1 mile from Gettysburg'. Tripp (11th Massachusetts, 27 Jul) and Bodine (26th Pennsylvania, 28 Jul), both of the First Brigade, wrote that they 'arrived at 2 a. m.' on the 2d. Fifteen years later Humphreys wrote privately that the division 'reached the ground towards midnight of July 1st'. All four are of the best class of writing, present with their units, on the Union clock, and the hours differ by an hour or two. The three hours may well be three moments of one march (head, middle and tail of a column, a brigade's front, a regiment's halt), but the sources do not say which regiment led or what each hour marks, so no one is preferred to the others on the rubric. The record is divided: the window about midnight to 2 a.m. is the default; Humphreys's 1 a.m. is inside it. The plan's midnight and 02:00 are both sourced and neither is struck. The later books that say 1 a.m. name no source and are counted with Humphreys's report. The third brigade is a separate event at 09:00 (Humphreys and Burling).
weighing.who: Humphreys commanded the division; Brewster the Second (Excelsior) Brigade; Tripp and Bodine commanded two regiments of Carr's First Brigade, each reporting for his own unit. Burling commanded the third brigade, which was left at Emmitsburg. Bachelder (1873, 1878), the New York commission (1900) and the 1913 Meade volume were not present and name no source.
weighing.when: Tripp's report is dated 27 Jul 1863 (26 days after), Bodine's 28 Jul, Brewster's 15 Aug (45 days), Humphreys's 16 Aug (46 days), Burling's 20 Aug; Humphreys's letter to Fitz Lee is from before early 1878 (14 to 15 years later); the books are 10 to 50 years later. The four reports of 1863 are of the same rank.
weighing.where: Each officer stood with his own unit: Tripp and Bodine with their regiments, Brewster with the Second Brigade, Humphreys with the division on the march after the detour near the Black Horse Tavern. The hours therefore describe different units and different moments (a regiment's arrival, a brigade reaching a point, the division's settling into bivouac a mile from Gettysburg, east of the Emmitsburg road); no one says which unit led. Whether Humphreys's 'reached the ground' of 1878 is the head of the column is not stated.
weighing.how_knew: Tripp, Bodine and Brewster each report their own unit's march: eyewitness or own orders, with round hours ('2 a. m.', 'about midnight'). Humphreys: his own division, own orders, round hour. The letter is a recollection. The later books give no basis.
weighing.clock: All four are Union writers and use plain hours without saying whose watch; no clock correction is applied, and the plan's note of about 20 minutes between the armies' clocks plays no part for Union witnesses. The round hours ('1 a. m.', '2 a. m.') may stand for the quarter or half hour around them; Brewster's is 'about'.
weighing.independence: Four lines of knowledge for the window: Brewster; Humphreys's report; Tripp; Bodine (Tripp and Bodine served in one brigade and may have received the same order or taken the hour from one brigade log, but each wrote his own report, and are counted as two groups). Humphreys's letter and Bachelder's 1873 'midnight' are one other line (Bachelder gives no source and may have had it from Humphreys). Bachelder's letter of 1878, the New York volume and the 1913 book repeat 1 a.m. and are treated as dependent on Humphreys's report; that is an assumption, not shown (they name no source). The 09:00 junction of the third brigade is independent: Humphreys and Burling are two reports.

source_panel_text: Between about midnight and 2 a.m. on Jul 2. Four officers of the division wrote in 1863: Brewster has his brigade arriving about midnight, Humphreys has the division bivouacking at 1 a.m., and Tripp and Bodine of two regiments say 2 a.m. No source says which unit led, so the window stays. The brigade left at Emmitsburg joined at 9 a.m.
